sourceTracingAudit.method: An input corpus is worth what its fidelity is worth, so every state was traced to the clause its source field names, and the mapping from evidence members to states was checked for both invention and omission.
sourceTracingAudit.packIdentity: This was the sharpest probe. State one's stateNamed contains 'a pack other than opensip.preview.typescript.pack version 1 (wrong name, wrong version, or a non-bundled identity)' — a fully specific pack name and version, which is precisely what a corpus inventing the future DR-131 pack would look like. It is not invented: G24 v1's EV-1 exactByteIntent carries that string, parenthetical included, and the state quotes it. Verified by substring containment against the source rather than by reading.
sourceTracingAudit.ev3SplitIntoTwo: EV-3 requires bytes that 'supply a user pack or a third-party pack' and pins 'the supplied-pack provenance (user or third-party)'. The corpus makes two states, one per provenance. That is the source's own signal — the fixture must distinguish which provenance it presents — so the split is faithful rather than inflating the count.
sourceTracingAudit.ev1KeptWhole: EV-1's parenthetical lists three variants joined by 'or', glossing one condition. The corpus keeps them inside one state's stateNamed rather than making three states. That also tracks the source's signal, and the contrast with G07 is the reason I am satisfied with both: G07's EV-1 says 'a typed refusal record for each file-04 hazard class', which mandates per-class records and where I credited an eight-way split; this clause says bytes that name a pack other than X, with the parenthetical describing how that one condition arises. Nothing is lost either way, since the parenthetical is carried verbatim.

sourceTracingAudit.memberCoverage: G24 v1 holds exactly three retained-evidence members, EV-1, EV-2 and EV-3, and the four states cite all three with no member unrepresented and no state citing a member that does not exist.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Eighteen attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject b279a615 at 0444, 5521 bytes, unmoved at both ends; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and the artifact's head equals it; live required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified. All five cited pins reproduce and the artifact's five 64-hex strings are exactly those pins. Four named initial states across three evidence members, and the review turned on fidelity rather than on presence. The sharpest probe was the pack identity: state one's stateNamed contains 'a pack other than opensip.preview.typescript.pack version 1 (wrong name, wrong version, or a non-bundled identity)', a fully specific pack name and version, which is exactly what a corpus inventing the future DR-131 pack would look like at a glance. It is not invented — G24 v1's EV-1 exactByteIntent carries that string with its parenthetical, and I checked by containment against the source rather than by impression. The other three states trace the same way: EV-3's 'user pack or a third-party pack' becomes two states because EV-3 pins the supplied-pack provenance as one or the other, and EV-2's 'pack or contribution bytes that are not declarative-only' appears verbatim. All three of G24 v1's evidence members are represented and no state cites a member that does not exist. One judgment call is worth recording for consistency: EV-1's parenthetical names three variants and the corpus keeps them in a single state rather than splitting them. I accepted an eight-way split of G07's EV-1 an hour earlier, and the difference is in the source construction — G07 says 'a typed refusal record for each file-04 hazard class', which mandates per-class records, while this clause glosses one condition with alternatives joined by or. The standard in both is to follow the source's own signal, and here the parenthetical is carried verbatim so nothing is lost. The boundaries hold. D-150's adopted text confirms DR-G24 owns DR-131 NT-1 and NT-2 only and closes their leftover-design, which the corpus reports accurately and does not reopen; the same passage leaves other NT classes elsewhere and the corpus takes none of them. G23, G29 and G30 each occur exactly twice, both times in refusals, matching the disclaimers EV-1, EV-2 and EV-3 carry themselves. Pack IR is refused four times with no IR node, grammar or evaluation rule present, and ARCH.PROBE-CONTRACT is not carried at all so no discharge is implied. All four states are NOT-AUTHORED, there are zero fixture paths, and the gate join holds OBL-G24-FX-AUTHORING at leftoverDesign true on DR-G24. Disclosure: both Claude-lane verdicts this corpus pins are my lane's and I accepted the G24 harness earlier today, and I set the standard this family is measured against in the G16 verdict, now applied five times with three rejections and two acceptances. The risk at this point is settling into a quick sort by whether states look populated, so I made the fidelity checks the substance of the review rather than the presence of content.
